items.title: OpenAI teases Astra, its next major model, via ten solved open math problems
items.summary: OpenAI revealed on August 1 that an internal version of Astra — described as its "next major model family," built to coordinate multiple agents on a problem for hours or days — generated verified solutions to ten long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, including a non-sofic group construction and three Erdős problems, each unsolved for at least a decade. Every proof ships with a zero-"sorry" Lean 4 formalization on GitHub, and OpenAI says the total compute cost across all ten was about $2,000 at Sol API rates.
items.whyItMatters: Astra is pitched as a long-horizon, multi-agent reasoning model rather than a chat model — worth watching for whether that architecture (or a distilled version) could eventually power deeper lesson-planning or error-diagnosis reasoning behind Romain/Anna, separate from the realtime voice layer itself.

items.title: Microsoft's agentic security system Project Perception enters public preview
items.summary: Project Perception, Microsoft's AI cybersecurity platform first detailed July 27, opened public preview on August 3. It coordinates red (attack-path mapping), blue (risk triage), and green (remediation) agent teams alongside a new in-house model, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, which Microsoft says scores 96% on the CyberGym benchmark — 12 points ahead of Anthropic's Mythos — at roughly half the cost by routing most work to a cheaper specialist model and escalating only hard cases.
items.whyItMatters: The task-routed, cheap-specialist-first architecture (and the red/blue/green agent split) is a reusable cost pattern for any Romain/Anna pipeline step that doesn't need a frontier model on every turn.

items.title: Yellow.ai to go public via $550M SPAC merger, powered by its Nexus Vox voice agents
items.summary: Enterprise agentic-AI company Yellow.ai announced on August 3 a definitive merger with Bluerock Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: BLRK) that will take it public at a roughly $550M pro forma equity value, with over $200M in expected gross proceeds. The release names Nexus Vox — low-latency, human-like voice agents in 135+ languages — as Yellow.ai's fastest-growing product, handling a share of the company's 16 billion annual conversations.
items.whyItMatters: A public listing built around a 135-language low-latency voice-agent product is a market signal that enterprise buyers now expect real-time multilingual voice as table stakes — the same bar Romain and Anna are competing against outside the language-learning niche.
